source_content.content: ### 4.1 Experimental Setup Models. We evaluate LKV on two widely adopted open-weights models: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct*(Grattafiori et al., [2024](#bib.bib14 ""))* and Qwen3-8B*(Yang et al., [2025](#bib.bib38 ""))*. Both models inherently employ GQA for efficient inference. Crucially, our method is fully compatible with the GQA structure and achieves significant further compression on top of these already efficient architectures, adding only $\sim$0.1% trainable parameters (see architecture details in Appendix[C.1](#A3.SS1 "C.1 Model Architecture and Parameter Efficiency ‣ Appendix C Training Implementation Details ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction")). #### Benchmarks. To evaluate the quality of compression, we adopt two standard benchmarks. LongBench*(Bai et al., [2024](#bib.bib3 ""))* is used as our primary benchmark for understanding long-contexts, where we select 16 representative subtasks. See Appendix[D.1](#A4.SS1 "D.1 Benchmark Filtering and Configuration ‣ Appendix D Evaluation Setup Details ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction") for detailed configurations and filtering criteria. We further evaluate on RULER*(Hsieh et al., [2024](#bib.bib15 ""))*, a synthetic benchmark that systematically probes model performance under compressed long-context inputs across varying sequence lengths and task complexities. #### Training Details. LKV is trained via self-distillation on our Loom dataset ($\sim$23k samples), strictly decontaminated from evaluation benchmarks (see Appendix[C.2](#A3.SS2 "C.2 Training Data Construction ‣ Appendix C Training Implementation Details ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction")). The process is cost-effective, taking $<2$ hours on $8\times$A100 GPUs (hyperparameters in Appendix[C.3](#A3.SS3 "C.3 Hyperparameters and Training Schedule ‣ Appendix C Training Implementation Details ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction")). #### Baselines. Implemented via KVPress*(Devoto et al., [2025](#bib.bib7 ""))*, we compare LKV against Full Cache and several baselines: SnapKV*(Li et al., [2024a](#bib.bib19 ""))* (uniform budgets); PyramidKV*(Cai et al., [2025](#bib.bib5 ""))* (layer-wise budget decay); DuoAttention*(Xiao et al., [2024](#bib.bib37 ""))* (offline optimized head patterns); and AdaKV*(Feng et al., [2025b](#bib.bib9 ""))* (specifically Ada-SnapKV, in-layer adaptive budgeting). Additionally, Expected Attention (ExpAttn)*(Devoto et al., [2025](#bib.bib7 ""))* is included for component analysis. All experiments follow a question-agnostic*(Feng et al., [2025b](#bib.bib9 ""))* setup, where the question is unavailable during context compression. ### 4.2 General Long-Context Capabilities We evaluate the comprehensive capabilities of LKV on LongBench. Table[1](#S4.T1 "Table 1 ‣ Robustness across Budgets. ‣ 4.2 General Long-Context Capabilities ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction") presents the comparison against representative baselines on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct under a strict 15% KV budget ($R\=0.15$); for the complete task-wise breakdown, please refer to Table[8](#A5.T8 "Table 8 ‣ E.1 Detailed LongBench Breakdown ‣ Appendix E Additional Experimental Results ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction"). Figure[3](#S4.F3 "Figure 3 ‣ Robustness across Budgets. ‣ 4.2 General Long-Context Capabilities ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction") visualizes the performance trends across varying retention ratios. #### Overall Performance Comparison. LKV achieves an average score of 46.73, consistently outperforming representative baselines. It recovers 98.4% of the Full Cache performance (46.73 vs. 47.48), demonstrating virtually lossless context retention. Compared to the strongest heuristic baseline, Ada-SnapKV, our method leads by a substantial margin of 7.67 points. This gap highlights the structural advantage of our approach: while heuristic methods relying on local statistics often misallocate resources, LKV learns a global budgeting policy that directly aligns with the generation objective. We observe consistent superiority on Qwen3-8B as well, with detailed results provided in Table[9](#A5.T9 "Table 9 ‣ E.1 Detailed LongBench Breakdown ‣ Appendix E Additional Experimental Results ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction"). #### Overcoming Rigid Priors. A key advantage of LKV is its ability to break free from hand-crafted structural constraints. Baselines like PyramidKV and DuoAttention enforce pre-defined patterns—specifically, a rigid layer-wise decay or a fixed offline binary classification. As shown in Table[1](#S4.T1 "Table 1 ‣ Robustness across Budgets. ‣ 4.2 General Long-Context Capabilities ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction"), these methods suffer severe degradation on retrieval-intensive tasks. For instance, in the Synthetic category (heavily impacted by the Passage Retrieval task, see full breakdown in Table[8](#A5.T8 "Table 8 ‣ E.1 Detailed LongBench Breakdown ‣ Appendix E Additional Experimental Results ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction")), DuoAttention and PyramidKV drop to 17.75 and 24.99, respectively. These rigid priors aggressively prune deep layers or specific heads that are critical for retrieving specific information. In contrast, LKV achieves a high score of 53.38 (matching Full Cache) by automatically identifying and preserving these critical capacities. #### Learned vs. Heuristic Adaptation. Although Ada-SnapKV introduces adaptivity, its marginal improvement over the uniform SnapKV baseline (39.06 vs. 38.05) exposes the fundamental limitations of heuristic-based allocation. First, Ada-SnapKV relies on attention concentration as a proxy for budget demand. This heuristic is insufficient because a head’s concentration pattern does not necessarily correlate with its task importance, especially when the method is still constrained by a rigid uniform layer-wise budget. It fails to reallocate resources across layers to preserve deep-context information. Second, the underlying token selection still depends on accumulated attention scores, which rely on historical statistics rather than predicting future retrieval needs. LKV overcomes these dual barriers by learning a global policy that directly optimizes the generation objective, unrestricted by layer boundaries or heuristic proxies. #### Robustness across Budgets. Figure[3](#S4.F3 "Figure 3 ‣ Robustness across Budgets. ‣ 4.2 General Long-Context Capabilities ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction") illustrates the performance consistency of LKV on both Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen3-8B models. Our method consistently maintains a superior performance-efficiency trade-off compared to baselines. Notably, the performance advantage remains highly significant as the budget decreases (e.g., at 10% budget). This demonstrates that LKV is also exceptionally robust in extreme low-resource regimes. (a) Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (b) Qwen3-8B† *Figure 3: Performance on LongBench across varying KV cache retention ratios.LKV shows robustness in low-resource regimes.* †For Qwen3, we employ an on-the-fly approximation due to the lack of official pre-computed patterns. (see Appendix[D.2](#A4.SS2 "D.2 Baseline Implementation Details ‣ Appendix D Evaluation Setup Details ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction")) *Table 1: Main Results on LongBench (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct). Evaluated under 15% KV budget ($R\=0.15$).* | Method | Avg. | Single-Doc. QA | Multi-Doc. QA | Summarization | Few-Shot | Synthetic | Code | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Full Cache | 47.48 | 43.57 | 45.41 | 28.89 | 65.43 | 53.48 | 51.42 | | SnapKV | 38.05 | 27.27 | 34.08 | 22.93 | 58.11 | 40.73 | 50.05 | | PyramidKV | 32.12 | 25.17 | 26.75 | 22.57 | 49.29 | 24.99 | 46.29 | | DuoAttention | 31.03 | 21.76 | 25.94 | 21.66 | 50.71 | 17.75 | 50.40 | | Ada-SnapKV | 39.06 | 27.38 | 35.46 | 23.29 | 59.28 | 43.77 | 50.56 | | LKV (Ours) | 46.73 | 41.66 | 42.79 | 28.76 | 66.30 | 53.38 | 51.25 | ### 4.3 Robustness to Context Length and Compression We further evaluate the robustness of LKV on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct by varying the context length $t$ and the global retention ratio $R$. The results are visualized in Figure[4](#S4.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ Performance under Extreme Compression. ‣ 4.3 Robustness to Context Length and Compression ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction"). Results on Qwen models show consistent trends and are visualized in Figure[6](#A5.F6 "Figure 6 ‣ E.2 Qwen3-8B performance on RULER benchmark ‣ Appendix E Additional Experimental Results ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction"). #### Scalability to Long Contexts. Figure[4](#S4.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ Performance under Extreme Compression. ‣ 4.3 Robustness to Context Length and Compression ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction")(a) demonstrates performance stability as context extends from 4k to 32k ($R\=0.15$). Despite training within 16k, LKV generalizes robustly to unseen lengths (32k). We attribute this to the learned policy’s transferability: LKV-H captures intrinsic head patterns (e.g., sparse or dense) that remain consistent across lengths, while LKV-T derives token utility strictly from the KV states themselves. Interestingly, baselines like SnapKV exhibit a slight artifactual rebound at 32k. This arises because the fixed ratio implies a doubled absolute capacity (e.g., $\sim$4.8k tokens), offering a larger buffer for heuristics to capture scattered information by chance. Nevertheless, LKV consistently outperforms these methods by a significant margin. #### Performance under Extreme Compression. Figure[4](#S4.F4 "Figure 4 ‣ Performance under Extreme Compression. ‣ 4.3 Robustness to Context Length and Compression ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction")(b) evaluates performance on fixed length inputs ($t\=16k$) across varying retention ratios (from 0.5 down to 0.1). The advantage of LKV becomes more pronounced in low-resource regimes. Even when the retention ratio is reduced to $R\=0.1$, LKV retains a high degree of performance. While AdaKV performs better than rigid priors (e.g., PyramidKV, DuoAttention) due to its adaptive nature, it still lags behind LKV under extreme compression. Structural priors like DuoAttention experience significant degradation at lower ratios, failing to adapt their rigid head-pruning strategies to tight budgets. This confirms that LKV utilizes the limited budget more effectively than both heuristic adaptive methods and static priors. (a) Varying Length ($R\=0.15$) (b) Varying Ratio ($t\=16k$) *Figure 4: Robustness evaluation on RULER (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct).* ### 4.4 Ablation Study: Dissecting the Gains To disentangle the contributions of budget allocation (LKV-H) and token selection (LKV-T), we conduct a comprehensive grid analysis on LongBench using Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (15% budget). We combine three budgeting strategies (Uniform, AdaKV, LKV-H) with three token selection policies: SnapKV, LKV-T, and ExpAttn, a recent method that selects tokens by estimating their expected future attention. Table[2](#S4.T2 "Table 2 ‣ Superiority of LKV-T Selector. ‣ 4.4 Ablation Study: Dissecting the Gains ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction") reports the macro-average score (Avg.) across all 16 subtasks, along with results on representative retrieval-intensive subsets. #### Dominance of Learned Budgeting (LKV-H). The results reveal that budget allocation is the primary driver of performance. While heuristic adaptation (AdaKV) provides only marginal gains over the Uniform baseline, our learned policy (LKV-H) delivers massive improvements across all selectors. For instance, LKV-H boosts ExpAttn by +8.60 points on average. Crucially, under uniform budgeting, ExpAttn suffers catastrophic failure on retrieval-heavy tasks (e.g., 17.77 on Synthetic); however, LKV-H acts as a universal enhancer, rescuing it to 45.00. We observe consistent gains on real-world tasks like Multi-Doc QA (e.g., +7.67 gain for SnapKV), proving that LKV-H effectively corrects the flaws of heuristic selectors. #### Superiority of LKV-T Selector. Comparing the columns in Table[2](#S4.T2 "Table 2 ‣ Superiority of LKV-T Selector. ‣ 4.4 Ablation Study: Dissecting the Gains ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction"), our LKV-T selector consistently outperforms existing methods. Under the Uniform budget, LKV-T achieves 39.74, surpassing both SnapKV (38.05) and ExpAttn (37.12). When combined with our learned budget, the full LKV system achieves the highest average score of 46.73. This confirms that LKV-T provides a highly accurate yet efficient (Matrix-free) selection mechanism. *Table 2: Impact of different budgeting and selection strategy combinations. Evaluated on LongBench (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct) under 15% KV budget.* | Selection | Budgeting | Avg. | $\Delta_{Base}$ | Multi-Doc QA | Synthetic | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | SnapKV | Uniform | 38.05 | - | 34.08 | 40.73 | | | AdaKV | 39.06 | +1.01 | 35.46 | 43.77 | | \cellcolorgray!10LKV-H | 44.06 | +6.01 | 41.75 | 52.87 | | ExpAttn | Uniform | 37.12 | - | 37.39 | 17.77 | | | AdaKV | 38.16 | +1.04 | 37.33 | 23.26 | | \cellcolorgray!10LKV-H | 45.72 | +8.60 | 43.27 | 45.00 | | LKV-T | Uniform | 39.74 | - | 40.27 | 22.41 | | | AdaKV | 43.45 | +3.71 | 38.83 | 47.76 | | \cellcolorgray!10LKV-H | 46.73 | +6.99 | 42.79 | 53.38 | ### 4.5 Overhead and Memory Analysis We analyze the computational overhead and memory efficiency of LKV during the prefill phase of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct ($R\=0.15$) on A100-80G. To accurately measure storage benefits, we employ a custom implementation using flash_attn_varlen_func *(Dao et al., [2022](#bib.bib6 ""))*, which flattens the compressed KV cache into a compact format to eliminate padding overhead. #### Eviction Overhead and Complexity. Table[3](#S4.T3 "Table 3 ‣ Memory Efficiency. ‣ 4.5 Overhead and Memory Analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction") compares the prefill latency at 200k context length (the maximum supported by Full Cache). DuoAttention achieves the lowest latency due to its static head pruning strategy ($O(1)$ selection complexity). In comparison, LKV employs a lightweight MLP for dynamic token selection ($O(T)$ complexity). The measured overhead is marginal: compared to the Full Cache baseline (82.40s), LKV incurs roughly a 7.7% increase in latency (88.76s). This is comparable to AdaKV (88.37s), which also performs dynamic filtering. Considering the significant gains in downstream task performance and memory capacity, this minor construction cost is a favorable trade-off. #### Memory Efficiency. Figure[5](#S4.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ Memory Efficiency. ‣ 4.5 Overhead and Memory Analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction") dissects the memory consumption across context lengths. First, regarding system stability, Full Cache exhibits rapid memory growth, crashing with OOM errors at 225k tokens. In contrast, LKV successfully scales to 262k and beyond. This capability stems from the aggressive compression of the KV tensors (Figure[5](#S4.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ Memory Efficiency. ‣ 4.5 Overhead and Memory Analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction")b). By maintaining a 15% budget, LKV reduces the actual storage cost at 200k length from 25.0 GB (Full) to 3.75 GB (Ours), achieving a 6.6$\times$ reduction. It is worth noting that the reduction in total peak memory (Figure[5](#S4.F5 "Figure 5 ‣ Memory Efficiency. ‣ 4.5 Overhead and Memory Analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction")a) appears less aggressive than the storage compression ratio. This is because the peak footprint is dominated by static model weights and transient activation buffers, which partially mask the savings from the compressed KV cache. Nevertheless, the substantial reduction in KV storage is sufficient to extend the maximum context length significantly beyond the hardware limit of Full Cache. (a) Peak Memory (b) KV Cache Size *Figure 5: Memory profiling on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct ($R\=0.15$).* *Table 3: Eviction complexity and prefill latency comparison at 200k context length. $W$ denotes the observation window size, and $T$ represents the context length.* | Method | Complexity | Time (s) | Overhead | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Full Cache | - | 82.40 | - | | DuoAttention | $O(1)$ | 87.21 | +5.8% | | Ada-SnapKV | $O(W\cdot T)$ | 88.37 | +7.2% | | LKV (Ours) | $O(T)$ | 88.76 | +7.7% |
